task.name: Baseline measurement of the current jlink image
Compute the truly-required module set via jdeps

comment.message: De-risk complete. Root cause found: java.desktop pulled by 'requires java.desktop' in jaxb-runtime + jackson-databind; jlink honors it unconditionally (--limit-modules probe could NOT drop it). shipsmooth uses neither AWT nor java.beans, and its JAXB-bound model has no Image/DataHandler fields, so the desktop-backed branch is unreachable. Lever for Task 3 = patch requires out of those two module-info descriptors (re-jar). Expected ~6-9M saving (desktop+prefs+datatransfer+~5.7M native AWT libs).

Abandoned: investigation (Tasks 1-2) showed the realistic jlink-only saving on OpenJ9 is ~9-12MB and the 87MB floor is dominated by the OpenJ9 runtime itself, not modules. Decision was to capture findings in docs/observations rather than implement the cut in this plan.
Abandoned: deferred with Task 3; no implementation undertaken in this plan.

task.name: Find online information about IBM Semeru JDK floor size

comment.message: Done. Findings added to docs/observations/2026-06-14-jlink-image-size-runtime-breakdown.md (section: Public corroboration). OpenJ9 issue #4488 confirms OpenJ9 jlink images carry a ~10-15MB premium over HotSpot (Java 11: Linux 52.6 vs 46.8MB; Windows 50.6 vs 38.0MB), accepted upstream (Deep Backlog). IBM publishes no official jlink floor figure for Semeru; their size guidance is JRE-vs-JDK container images, a different question.

update.message: Plan complete. Investigation delivered (Tasks 1,2,6 closed): jlink image-size analysis captured in docs/observations/2026-06-14-jlink-image-size-runtime-breakdown.md. Implementation tasks (3,4,5: prune java.desktop, size flags, regression guard) abandoned after findings showed the 87MB floor is dominated by the OpenJ9 runtime, not modules; realistic jlink-only saving ~9-12MB. Reaching ~45MB requires an OpenJ9->HotSpot switch, out of scope here.
